title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
blurb: Showed that the KL-regularised RLHF objective can be optimised directly from preference pairs with a classification loss, with no reward model and no RL loop.
intro: The optimal policy for a KL-penalised reward has a closed form, so the reward can be written in terms of the policy's log-probability ratio to a reference model. Substituting that into the Bradley-Terry preference likelihood cancels the intractable normaliser and leaves a loss on the policy alone. The steps build preference data, the Bradley-Terry loss, the DPO loss from token log-probabilities and the choice of length normalisation; the capstone computes sequence log-probabilities for a bigram model and takes one DPO gradient step.
